transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. I came in because, honestly, I feel like I’m crawling out of my skin whenever I’m supposed to just sit still. It happens a lot in the radiology suite or when I'm in a classroom. I've been trying to just tough it out for months now, but... I don't know, I still just end up pacing, shifting around in my chair, or finding some random excuse to get up and move. I just can't seem to stop.
Have you started or changed any medications recently, particularly antipsychotics, anti-nausea drugs, or other prescriptions, around the time these restless feelings began?
No, I haven't. I don't actually take any of those... or really any prescriptions at all, honestly. So I haven't started or changed any medications recently.
Have you experienced this kind of restlessness and difficulty sitting still since childhood, or is this something that started more recently, say within the past several months?

No, it's definitely not a recent thing. It's been going on since I was little. My parents actually still talk about my elementary school conferences... they said the teachers were always telling them that I was constantly out of my seat, calling out, or just rushing ahead before they even finished giving directions. So, yeah, this was happening way before middle school, definitely not just since I started my radiology training.
